record.title: An Algebraic Approach to Quantum Field Theory
record.version: Journal of Mathematical Physics 5(7), 848-861 (1964); DOI 10.1063/1.1704187
record.section_locator: Abstract; pp. 848-861; scanned primary PDF text checked at https://electronicsandbooks.com/edt/manual/Magazine/J/Journal%20of%20Mathematical%20Physics/PDF/V05/JMP1964V05N07.pdf
record.assumptions: Axiomatic algebraic formulation assigning algebras of observables to spacetime regions; the article discusses isotony, locality and covariance in a fixed Minkowski setting. The exact conventional net axiom list was not fully transcribed from the scanned copy in this pass.
record.conclusion: Advocates local observable algebras as the central structure and argues that faithful representations of the same abstract observable algebra can express physical equivalence despite unitary inequivalence. The framework encodes which observables are local and their inclusion/commutation relations; it does not specify a temporal ontology or passage.
record.proof_status: Conceptual framework paper; no theorem proof independently reconstructed.
dependencies: Mathematical setting: abstract observable *-algebras and their faithful Hilbert-space representations; assignment of observable algebras to spacetime regions and the stated locality/covariance structure. These are the framework's own ingredients, not an externally audited theorem dependency.
record.open_questions: A later exact axiom-by-axiom extraction from Haag (1996) or a primary formalization would be useful; no such claim is needed for this lane.
record.relevance: Baseline locality/net model and limits of what local algebra structure alone says about time.
record.limits: Full scanned article text was available, but some OCR/math is noisy. Do not read the source as proving that locality entails eternalism, presentism, or objective becoming. No relevant related source record in this lane is an input to the paper; related_source_ids is therefore intentionally empty.

record.title: Bemerkungen zur unitäräquivalenz von lorentzinvarianten Feldern
record.version: Il Nuovo Cimento 22(5), 1051-1068 (1961); DOI 10.1007/BF02787889 verified against MaRDI/zbMATH metadata, text unread
record.relevance: Original Reeh–Schlieder source for vacuum cyclicity and the nontrivial limits on interpreting local operations as producing spatially localized states.
record.limits: Original full text not obtained; bibliographic lead only. The theorem assumptions below are taken from the full-text later exposition aqft-fewster-rejzner-2020v2, not attributed to an unaudited exact statement in this original.

record.title: Algebraic Quantum Field Theory – an introduction
record.version: arXiv:1904.04051v2, 18 November 2019; published in Progress and Visions in Quantum Theory in View of Gravity (Birkhäuser, 2020)
record.section_locator: Sec. 4.1 basic AQFT requirements; Sec. 5.2, Theorem 26 and proof, pp. 25-27 of v2 PDF; Sec. 6.3 local experiments can be prepared locally
record.assumptions: For the Reeh–Schlieder theorem as stated in Sec. 5.2: a Poincaré-covariant Haag–Kastler net in a vacuum representation, positive-energy/spectrum condition, translation-invariant vacuum cyclic for the global algebra, weak additivity, and a nonempty region with a smaller open region whose sufficiently small translates remain inside. Einstein causality plus an open region in the causal complement gives separation. Full precise statement is source-located; hypotheses summarized here rather than independently formalized.
record.conclusion: The vacuum is cyclic for each such local algebra; if the causal complement has interior and Einstein causality holds, it is also separating. Cyclicity means norm-approximation of arbitrary Hilbert vectors by AΩ with A in the local algebra, not that an implementable, energy-bounded, deterministic, or no-signaling operation locally prepares an arbitrary distant state. Sec. 6.3 distinguishes state-vector approximation from local experiment preparation and uses extra operational structure.
record.proof_status: Authors provide a proof in the cited section; statement and proof section inspected, not independently reproduced.
dependencies: Reeh–Schlieder derivation uses Poincaré covariance, positive-energy translation spectrum, invariant vacuum, global cyclicity, weak additivity and local commutativity as stated in Sec. 5.2; separation additionally uses a nonempty causal complement. These are theorem premises, not a new result.
record.open_questions: Theorem versions vary in region regularity and additivity assumptions; any use beyond the stated vacuum-net hypotheses needs an exact matching result. Quantitative cost/energy bounds are not supplied by cyclicity alone.
record.relevance: Provides explicit Reeh–Schlieder assumptions and distinguishes cyclicity from operationally implementable local experiments.
record.limits: Pedagogical exposition of established theory rather than an original proof paper. The authors explicitly say algebraic states need not all be physically realizable (Sec. 2.3); no inference from dense orbit to superluminal signaling is licensed.

record.title: Tomita's Theory of Modular Hilbert Algebras and its Applications
record.version: Lecture Notes in Mathematics 128, Springer (1970); DOI 10.1007/BFb0065832
record.relevance: Foundational exposition of Tomita–Takesaki modular theory: for a von Neumann algebra with a cyclic and separating vector, the modular objects generate an intrinsic one-parameter automorphism group and identify the commutant via modular conjugation.
record.limits: Bibliographic and metadata discovery only in this lane; theorem statement and proof not directly audited from Takesaki. The algebraic theorem is stated in the inspected original Bisognano–Wichmann 1975 paper, pp. 998-999, and should be used as the exact locator here.

record.title: On the Duality Condition for a Hermitian Scalar Field
record.version: Journal of Mathematical Physics 16(4), 985-1007 (1975); DOI 10.1063/1.522605; scanned primary copy https://denebola.if.usp.br/~jbarata/leituras-recomendadas/BisognanoWichmann-01-DualityConditionHermitianScalarField_985_1_online.pdf
record.section_locator: Secs. II-IV, Theorems 1-2, especially pp. 990-998; modular-theory statement pp. 998-999; wedge-duality assumptions pp. 1000-1002
record.assumptions: The paper works in four-dimensional Minkowski space with a separable physical Hilbert space, strongly continuous unitary proper-Poincaré representation, translation spectrum in the closed forward cone, unique translation-invariant vacuum, and a local Hermitian scalar operator-valued tempered-distribution field. The modular-algebra conclusion additionally requires a wedge von Neumann algebra with vacuum cyclic and invariant under the wedge-preserving boosts; the authors explicitly say existence/adequate size of such algebras is not automatic under their minimal field assumptions (pp. 986, 1002). Exact 1975 result is formulated through analytic continuation of boosts and TCP, then the modular operator relation, not as a blanket claim for any AQFT net.
record.conclusion: For the right wedge, the modular flow in the vacuum representation is the Lorentz boost subgroup preserving the wedge, with convention-dependent 2π normalization; modular conjugation is tied to TCP/reflection. Wedge duality follows only under additional algebra-existence/density premises discussed in the paper. The modular parameter is a state-and-algebra-dependent automorphism parameter identified geometrically in this special setting; it is not generic observer clock time, a universal time coordinate, or objective passage.
record.proof_status: Original paper full text inspected, including assumptions, theorem statements, and caveats; proof not independently reconstructed. The generalized modern BW theorem for arbitrary nets is not audited here.
dependencies: Tomita's modular theorem for a von Neumann algebra with cyclic-separating vector supplies J and the modular unitary group (BW pp. 998-999); the physical identification additionally uses the paper's Poincaré representation, forward spectrum, vacuum, scalar-field locality/analyticity and wedge-algebra premises recorded in assumptions.
record.open_questions: Compare exact theorem variants for general Wightman fields, graded-local nets, curved spacetimes, and representations without BW property before transferring the conclusion.
record.relevance: Sharp test case for the difference between modular flow and physical clock time.
record.limits: The title concerns duality, and the field/algebra domain assumptions matter. No universal modular Hamiltonian/local geometric flow is implied for bounded regions or arbitrary states.

record.title: Algebraic quantum field theory in curved spacetimes
record.version: arXiv:1504.00586v1 (2015); chapter in Advances in Algebraic Quantum Field Theory, Birkhäuser (2015), DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-21353-8_4
record.section_locator: Secs. 2-3 (locally covariant functor, local covariance, Einstein causality and time-slice); Sec. 5 and Sec. 7.6 (partial Reeh–Schlieder transfer); Sec. 11.3 (natural states no-go)
record.assumptions: Models a theory as a covariant functor from globally hyperbolic, oriented and time-oriented spacetimes with causally convex isometric embeddings to unital *-algebras; supplements functoriality with Einstein causality and the time-slice axiom. Specific results require further named hypotheses; see individual theorem records/locators.
record.conclusion: Local covariance structures local observables across spacetimes and compatible embeddings; it does not select a preferred foliation or unique state. Cauchy morphisms encode dynamical equivalence between globally hyperbolic regions sharing Cauchy data. This is a precise covariance/locality framework, not a metaphysical theory of becoming.
record.proof_status: Full chapter text inspected selectively at the stated sections; individual theorem proof audits are separately marked below.
dependencies: Mathematical framework: the Loc/Alg functorial setup, causally convex isometric embeddings, Einstein causality and the time-slice property; the chapter explicitly builds on the BFV locally covariant framework. Individual results have additional hypotheses given at their own locators.
record.open_questions: What extra structure would empirically distinguish observer-limited records from a complete algebraic history is not addressed by the framework itself.
record.relevance: Curved-spacetime comparison model for local covariance, dynamics, and records.
record.limits: This source is a review chapter, not an original result paper. Functorial locality/time-slice assumptions encode causal propagation but do not by themselves imply a temporal ontology. Stable lane ID retains the original `2012` label but is misleading: this record is the 2015 arXiv 1504.00586v1 chapter.

record.title: Dynamical locality and covariance: What makes a physical theory the same in all spacetimes?
record.version: arXiv:1106.4785v3 (8 May 2012); Annales Henri Poincaré 13, 1613-1673 (2012)
record.section_locator: Secs. 2-3 definitions; Sec. 6, Definition 6.1 dynamical locality, Theorems 6.10 and 6.13; Theorem 6.13 proof, lines 1022-1045 in arXiv HTML v3
record.assumptions: Theorem 6.13: a dynamically local theory in the authors' Loc functor category has a natural state assignment compatible with every spacetime morphism; on some spacetime with noncompact Cauchy surfaces, that state's GNS representation is faithful and has the Reeh–Schlieder cyclicity property for every relatively compact region. Under these premises relative Cauchy evolution is trivial there. If extended locality also holds, the theory is equivalent to the trivial theory. Paper's definitions of Loc, timeslice, dynamical locality, and extended locality apply.
record.conclusion: Kinematic local subalgebras and dynamical local subalgebras (observables insensitive to metric perturbations in the causal complement) coincide in dynamically local theories. The conditional no-natural-state theorem constrains a covariant preferred state in all spacetimes, not local records or passage directly. The conclusion follows from covariance, local response and cyclicity premises; it is not a no-go for every state selection on a single spacetime.
record.proof_status: Theorem statement and proof inspected in primary text; proof not independently reconstructed. Exact condition that cyclicity, faithfulness, noncompact Cauchy surface, and extended locality each enter is recorded.
dependencies: Builds on the BFV locally covariant theory category and time-slice framework; uses kinematic local subobjects, relative Cauchy evolution under metric perturbations, dynamical locality, GNS representations, Reeh–Schlieder cyclicity and (for the final equivalence conclusion) extended locality. Theorem 6.13 premises are enumerated in this record.
record.open_questions: Test the theorem against specific state spaces and theories only after verifying dynamical locality and faithfulness; theorem does not decide whether objective becoming exists.
record.relevance: Main audited result linking covariance, localized dynamical response and state selection.
record.limits: Authors explicitly present SPASs principles as necessary, not exhaustive. No inference to ontology, determinism, a thermodynamic arrow, or observer-access limits follows.

record.title: Dynamical locality of the free scalar field
record.section_locator: Abstract; Sec. 4, Theorem 4.3 and adjacent construction/proof, lines 406-422 in arXiv HTML
record.assumptions: The paper defines the massless minimally coupled scalar theory modulo locally constant solutions, in the locally covariant framework, and distinguishes categories Loc (possibly disconnected spacetimes) and Loc_0 (connected spacetimes). The theorem is specific to that quotient model and those categories.
record.conclusion: The quotient massless scalar theory is dynamically local in Loc_0 for all spacetime dimensions n>=2 and in Loc for n>=3, but not in Loc at n=2. The authors exhibit the two-dimensional disconnected-spacetime topological obstruction; they conjecture adding topological charge as background may address it. This is a model/domain-specific locality result, not a universal claim about local events.
record.proof_status: Theorem 4.3 statement and explanatory derivation inspected; no independent reproduction.
dependencies: Uses the locally covariant functor/time-slice and relative-Cauchy-evolution framework, the classical minimally coupled Klein–Gordon solution space, its symplectic structure, and the quotient by locally constant solutions. The comparison target is kinematic versus dynamical localization as defined in the Fewster–Verch framework.
record.open_questions: The paper identifies topological charge as a conjectural diagnosis of the two-dimensional failure; keep the authors' conjecture separate from theorem content.
record.relevance: Concrete counterexample to treating kinematic and dynamical localization as automatically identical.
record.limits: Massless scalar quotient model only; do not generalize the dimensional exception to all AQFTs.

record.title: Boltzmann’s Approach to Statistical Mechanics
record.version: arXiv:cond-mat/0105242v1 (2001-05-11; only version); chapter in Chance in Physics: Foundations and Perspectives, Lecture Notes in Physics 574, Springer (2001)
record.locators: Secs. 1-3 and discussion of reversibility/typicality; arXiv full text inspected
record.assumptions: Classical microstate evolves under time-reversal-invariant mechanics; macrovariables induce Boltzmann macroregions and entropy S_B=k log phase-volume; probability/typicality is relative to a specified macroregion and measure.
record.conclusion: Goldstein presents Boltzmannian statistical mechanics as deriving typical macroscopic entropy increase from reversible microscopic dynamics plus a low-entropy macrostate and typicality reasoning. Time-reversal symmetry entails the corresponding two-sided entropy-rise issue for a generic low-entropy macrostate at a time; a one-sided observed arrow requires further temporal boundary information or an alternative cosmological model.
record.proof_status: Primary full text read for stated conceptual argument; no independent derivation or quantitative reproduction.
record.dependencies: Boltzmann macrostate entropy, phase-space measure, time-reversal symmetry; this paper is a conceptual exposition, not a cosmological model.
record.open_questions: Which cosmological macrovariables and measure are physically appropriate in general relativity, and how should the probability conditional on present records be fixed?
record.relevance: Baseline for separating reversible dynamics, statistical typicality, and a cosmological low-entropy boundary condition.
record.limits: The account does not uniquely specify gravitational entropy or establish an ontological direction of time. The macroscopic arrow is not objective passage.

record.title: Is the Hypothesis About a Low Entropy Initial State of the Universe Necessary for Explaining the Arrow of Time?
record.locators: Secs. 1-2 (Past Hypothesis and central-time alternatives); Secs. 3-5 (toy model, non-normalizable measure, present evidence); Secs. 6-8 (mathematical/evidential/theoretical reasoning and conclusion); Appendix A
record.assumptions: The standard route posits a low-entropy initial macrostate and typical microstate relative to its macroregion. Alternative Carroll-Chen/Barbour-Koslowski-Mercati models use reversible, measure-preserving/unitary dynamics and an unbounded expanding spatial volume, so entropy has no maximum; their typical histories have a central entropy minimum and arrows pointing away on both sides. The paper's toy model simplifies macrostate to a size variable.
record.conclusion: Authors argue that central-time models can be mathematically compatible with ordinary two-sided typical entropy increase because their cosmological measure is non-normalizable; they distinguish typical histories predicted by a theory from evidential inference conditioned on present records. This supports model-conditional thermodynamic arrows, not a universal claim that the Past Hypothesis is dispensable or that ontology follows.
record.proof_status: Primary HTML full text inspected at the listed sections; toy-model formulas and measure argument read but not independently reproduced. The authors explicitly leave further typicality/evidential questions open in the paper.
record.dependencies: Hamiltonian time reversal and volume preservation, Boltzmann entropy, measure/conditioning choices, Carroll-Chen and Barbour et al. cosmological proposals.
record.open_questions: Whether an infinite-volume/non-normalizable measure and the chosen observer-conditioning are physically justified; whether actual cosmology belongs to these model classes; whether competing coarse-grainings preserve the result.
record.relevance: Directly compares a low-entropy boundary-condition explanation with cosmological typicality models, while exposing the distinction between theoretical typicality and empirical/evidential inference.
record.limits: The toy model is not our universe; a non-normalizable measure does not supply ordinary normalized probabilities without additional choices. No conclusion about passage, determinism, eternalism, or presentism.

record.title: Singularities and Time-Asymmetry
record.version: In General Relativity: An Einstein Centenary Survey, eds. S. W. Hawking and W. Israel, Cambridge University Press (1979), pp. 581-638; scan inspected
record.locators: Chapter 12, pp. 613-615 on gravitational clumping, Weyl curvature, and entropy; pp. 629-632 on the proposed initial-singularity Weyl condition and its tentative status
record.assumptions: Penrose qualitatively associates gravitational clumping and gravitational entropy with increasing Weyl curvature; early matter/radiation may be close to thermal equilibrium while the initial spacetime geometry is specially constrained. The proposed condition is time-asymmetric and directed at initial, not final, singularities.
record.conclusion: Penrose proposes a low-Weyl-curvature condition at an initial singularity as a geometric boundary condition intended to account for the special low gravitational entropy and thereby the thermodynamic arrow. He states that no clear-cut integral formula for gravitational entropy was then known and that the hypothesis was vague with multiple possible formulations. It is a proposal, not a theorem or established entropy law.
record.proof_status: Primary chapter scan read at the cited pages; no independent mathematical verification. Penrose labels the hypothesis tentative and says complete details are not worked out at those locators.
record.dependencies: Classical general relativity and singularity models; qualitative gravitational entropy/Weyl-curvature correspondence; a time-asymmetric initial boundary condition.
record.open_questions: Which precise scalar/tensor condition defines WCH across singularity classes; whether Weyl curvature measures gravitational entropy in general; how quantum gravity or nonsingular cosmologies alter the boundary proposal.
record.relevance: Canonical cosmological proposal linking gravitational entropy and an arrow via an initial geometric constraint.
record.limits: Weyl curvature is not itself a generally established entropy functional. Even if a low-Weyl boundary condition explains an arrow, it does not select a temporal ontology or establish objective passage.

record.title: On the Weyl Curvature Hypothesis
record.locators: arXiv v4 abstract and journal metadata; full proof not inspected
record.assumptions: Stoica defines a class of quasi-regular singularities with an extended Einstein-equation framework and considers cosmological models in that class.
record.conclusion: Abstract claims the Weyl tensor vanishes at quasi-regular singularities in the stated framework, including an example generalizing FLRW while relaxing homogeneity and isotropy. This is a conditional mathematical result about that singularity class, not evidence that WCH is a universal physical law or that Weyl curvature is a complete entropy measure.
record.proof_status: Abstract-level only; theorem, definitions, and proof not audited. Bibliographic authorship/version/journal data checked against original arXiv record.
record.dependencies: Specific regularity assumptions on degenerate metrics/singularities and Stoica's extended Einstein-equation formulation.
record.open_questions: How broad is the quasi-regular class physically, how does it compare to generic singularity models, and what entropy interpretation is independently justified?
record.relevance: Shows that a mathematical vanishing-Weyl result is conditional on a chosen singularity class and must not be conflated with confirming Penrose's physical conjecture.
record.limits: No proof audit and no empirical or thermodynamic conclusion checked.

record.title: The ‘Past Hypothesis’: Not even false
record.version: Studies in History and Philosophy of Modern Physics 37(3) (2006), pp. 399-430
record.locators: Publisher abstract; article sections 5-9 described there but not read
record.assumptions: Critiques attempts to identify a low Boltzmann-entropy initial macrostate in classical general-relativistic cosmology; emphasizes that a usable entropy concept and phase-space measure must be defined before probability claims.
record.conclusion: Earman challenges the received claim that modern cosmology has completed Boltzmann's program: he argues initial Boltzmann entropy may be ill-defined or severely hobbled in relevant GR cosmologies, and that even a well-defined low initial entropy would not alone explain temporally asymmetric behavior of ordinary thermodynamic systems. This attacks a premise/bridge in the standard explanation; it is not a demonstration that no cosmological arrow exists.
record.proof_status: Author abstract only; the detailed model calculations and argument have not been inspected.
record.dependencies: General-relativistic cosmology, Boltzmann entropy and measure, cosmological boundary conditions.
record.open_questions: Which specific GR models make the Boltzmann entropy undefined or inadequate; what alternative entropy/account of local arrows survives those objections?
record.relevance: Major adversarial predecessor against treating the Past Hypothesis as already well-defined and sufficient in relativistic cosmology.
record.limits: Abstract is a lead, not verification of the detailed critique; do not present Earman's objections as a settled refutation.

record.title: Arrow(s) of Time without a Past Hypothesis
record.version: arXiv:1809.04646v2 (2019-01-10; v1 2018-09-12, v3 2020-07-13); published as a chapter in Statistical Mechanics and Scientific Explanation: Determinism, Indeterminism and Laws of Nature, ed. V. Allori, World Scientific (2020), pages unverified
record.locators: Secs. 1-4 (PH status, fluctuation/observer-selection problem and typicality); Sec. 5 (Newtonian gravity entropy model); Sec. 6 (relational shape-space comparison); conclusion
record.assumptions: Compare finite-entropy eternal fluctuation cosmologies, bounded-entropy young-universe models, and eternal unbounded-entropy Carroll/Chen or Newtonian-gravity/shape-space models. Typicality depends on dynamics, macrovariables, and measure. A Boltzmann-brain inference requires a cosmological measure and a rule for conditioning on observers/evidence.
record.conclusion: Authors argue that an eternal unbounded-entropy model can have typical U-shaped entropy histories and arrows on both sides of a central minimum without a fundamental Past Hypothesis, while finite-entropy fluctuation models face self-location/Boltzmann-brain difficulties. They distinguish this theoretical typicality question from inference from current evidence and from Barbour et al.'s relational gravitational arrow. These are model-based author arguments, not established descriptions of observed cosmology.
record.proof_status: Primary full text read at stated sections. Newtonian N-body asymptotic results and cited simulations are reported rather than independently reproduced; no proof or simulation audit performed.
record.dependencies: Carroll-Chen cosmology, Barbour-Koslowski-Mercati shape dynamics, Newtonian N-body gravity, Boltzmann entropy proposal, typicality/observer-conditioning.
record.open_questions: Is the measure well-defined and physically motivated; does Newtonian N-body gravity represent cosmology; what observer typicality/conditioning is warranted; can empirical observations distinguish these cosmological scenarios?
record.relevance: Provides a direct comparison of Past Hypothesis, typicality, gravitational entropy, and Boltzmann-brain reasoning while retaining alternatives.
record.limits: The Newtonian model is not relativistic cosmology; simulation evidence is not a general theorem; typicality does not yield a unique empirical probability without measure and reference-class choices. No ontology conclusion. Coordinator correction 2026-10-20: an earlier version string named Studies in History and Philosophy of Science Part B 69 (2020) as the venue; no record supports that. arXiv listing and PhilSci/library records point to the 2020 World Scientific volume instead.

record.title: Disturbing Implications of a Cosmological Constant
record.locators: Secs. 5-6, especially discussion of recurrence, fluctuation rates, anthropic weighting and unusual observer-compatible states
record.assumptions: Conditional holographic/casual-patch picture with positive cosmological constant, finite de Sitter entropy, recurrence, and statistical weighting over fluctuations. The argument depends on assumptions about cosmological constant, horizon complementarity, observer measures, and what counts as an observer-compatible history.
record.conclusion: Authors argue their assumptions imply recurrences and raise a typicality problem: observer-compatible fluctuations unlike the standard low-entropy cosmological history can dominate, making our observed history atypical. The paper predates common Boltzmann-brain terminology and does not establish a model-independent Boltzmann-brain theorem.
record.proof_status: Primary arXiv HTML full text inspected at the cited sections; conceptual conditional argument read, not independently verified. Numerical entropy estimates are reported by authors and are not adopted as facts here.

record.open_questions: Are the causal-patch and finite-dimensional assumptions correct; what is the measure over observers/histories; do later cosmological models avoid the atypical-observer result?
record.relevance: Early primary source for the observer-typicality problem now often discussed via Boltzmann brains.
record.limits: Highly conditional theoretical argument; observer measure and cosmological assumptions are contested. It concerns typicality and cosmology, not thermodynamic ontology or objective passage.

record.title: Observation of Time Reversal Violation in the B0 Meson System
authors: J. P. Lees et al. (BABAR Collaboration)
record.locators: arXiv abstract and publication metadata; analysis not audited
record.assumptions: BABAR uses entangled neutral B meson pairs and compares transitions related by time reversal under the experiment's state-tagging protocol.
record.conclusion: The collaboration reports direct T-violating parameters in neutral B meson transitions. Therefore the blanket statement that all fundamental dynamical laws are time-reversal invariant is false. This microscopic weak-interaction T violation does not by itself explain the macroscopic thermodynamic arrow or select a temporal ontology.
record.proof_status: Abstract-level; experimental methods, systematic checks, and statistical analysis not independently audited.
record.dependencies: Neutral B meson mixing/decay, entanglement, transition-state tagging, weak interactions.
record.open_questions: What is the quantitative contribution of microscopic T-violating processes to macroscopic irreversibility? The cosmological/thermodynamic arrow question remains separate.
record.relevance: Empirical counterexample to overgeneralized claims about time-reversal symmetry of all dynamical laws.
record.limits: A particle-transition asymmetry is not the thermodynamic arrow; abstract-only and no ontology consequence.

record.title: Gravity, Entropy, and Cosmology: In Search of Clarity
record.version: arXiv:0907.0659v1 (2009-07-03); British Journal for the Philosophy of Science 61(3) (2010), pp. 513-540
record.locators: Secs. 2-4, 7, 8-10 of primary HTML read by a subsequent reviewer in this task; Sec. 7, “Entropy increase from gravitation and nuclear fusion,” contains the matter-entropy decrease/radiation-compensation claim; key distinctions at Sec. 3 and revised principles/conclusion at Sec. 10. Original worker's earlier screening was abstract-level.
record.assumptions: Distinguishes gravity's dynamical effects on material macrostates from entropy attributed to gravitational field degrees of freedom. Argues in relevant cosmological regimes that local matter entropy and radiation, expansion-driven departure from equilibrium, and gravitational dynamics must be considered; black-hole entropy is a special case. Scope is the author's statistical-mechanical analysis, not a general quantum-gravity derivation.
record.conclusion: Wallace argues that collapse need not increase the collapsing matter's entropy: in his model discussion the matter's entropy can decrease while heat/radiation transfer increases total entropy. He says gravitational collapse is not generally the source of local second-law behavior; expansion and nuclear fusion matter to his account. He criticizes Earman's limitations as too strong because gravity can affect material statistical mechanics through dynamics even when field entropy is neglected. This is a substantive counterpoint, not a final resolution of the Past Hypothesis or a universal entropy formula.
record.proof_status: Primary arXiv HTML sections 2-4, 7-10 read in a subsequent reviewer pass after the initial abstract-only record; the specific matter/radiation statement is located in Sec. 7 (knowledge/audits/fulltext-spotcheck/foundations/findings.jsonl, source_id arrow-wallace-gravity-entropy-2009). Calculations and wider empirical claims not independently reproduced.
record.dependencies: Classical statistical mechanics of gravitating matter, expanding-universe thermodynamics, matter/radiation entropy, and distinctions between field entropy and dynamical influence.
record.open_questions: Which parts of Wallace's classical account generalize to broader relativistic/quantum cosmological models; what entropy functional is appropriate for the initial universe; how does the account compare to later gravitational entropy proposals?
record.relevance: Detailed adversarial counterpoint to both a simplistic Weyl=entropy identification and the claim that Earman's critique rules out cosmological entropy reasoning; also shows why gravitational dynamics can matter without assigning an entropy to the gravitational field.
record.limits: This is the author's argument in a bounded 2009 treatment; it does not settle all gravitational-entropy questions or establish a unique cosmological entropy. No independent calculation or contemporary model audit.

record.title: Uniqueness of Simultaneity
record.version: arXiv:gr-qc/0011050v1 (submitted 2000-11-14, report no. ZU-TH 25/00); published as Brit. J. Phil. Sci. 52(4):651-670 (2001), DOI 10.1093/bjps/52.4.651 (DOI cross-checked via Semantic Scholar record; journal ref stated on arXiv landing page)
record.section_locator: arXiv HTML v1: Req.1/Req.2 (absolute vs relative simultaneity, soundness criterion 'classes meet any physically realizable trajectory in at most one point'); Thm 1 (existence criterion: non-maximal stabilizers); Thm 2-3 (Galilei case: classes are planes or unions mod lambda; standard Galilean simultaneity unique); Thm 4 (no nontrivial ILor-invariant equivalence relation, hence no absolute simultaneity in Lorentzian case); Thm 5 (ILor_X classification for X = inertial frame: orthogonal hyperplanes, unions mod lambda, the line, unions of lattice points); Thm 6 (Einstein simultaneity unique relative to an inertial frame under Req.2); Thm 7 + Appendix (re-proof of Malament's uniqueness using Alexandrov's characterization of causal automorphisms); Sec. 5 (critique of Sarkar-Stachel proof gap: G-invariant partitions need not have G-invariant classes; onion/shell counterexamples when dilations are dropped)
record.assumptions: Flat spacetime R^4; simultaneity = equivalence relation; automorphism group Aut = inhomogeneous Galilei or inhomogeneous Lorentz group (proper orthochronous, no reflections, no dilations), motivated by affine structure + relativity principle + boost equivariance; X = single observer worldline or foliation by parallel timelike lines (inertial frame); invariance of the partition under the stabilizer Aut_X; soundness: classes meet physically realizable (timelike) trajectories at most once.
record.conclusion: Paper's claims: with Aut=ILor there is no nontrivial invariant equivalence relation at all (no absolute simultaneity); relative to an inertial frame with the soundness condition, Einstein simultaneity is unique; Malament's theorem is re-derived for the single-worldline case with causal automorphisms (which include dilations and time reflections). Section 5 exhibits additional invariant equivalence relations (concentric-shell 'onion' partitions, tilted half-cones) that appear once dilations or time reflections are dropped from the invariance group, and identifies the exact step where Sarkar-Stachel's uniqueness proof fails.

record.open_questions: Giulini uses the physical-symmetry group rather than causal automorphisms; the two choices give different classifications, and which group is 'correct' depends on prior commitments about what counts as given structure (his Sec. 1 fn 2 and Sec. 5). record.relevance: Systematic group-theoretic classification of simultaneity relations; pins down exactly which invariance-group choices give uniqueness. Direct predecessor for any assumption-dependency graph of simultaneity.

record.conclusion: Theorem 2.1: the complex measure on the finite-stage algebra has a unique extension to the generated sigma-algebra iff it is of bounded variation. Theorem 3.1/Corollary 3.6: bounded variation if sum of zeta_n^a converges; not of bounded variation if sum of zeta_n^c diverges (antichain and chain nodes give the max and min, Lemmas 3.4-3.5). Claim 3.9: a countable family with asymptotically collinear couplings extends. Complex percolation extends only for q in [0,1] (Eqs. (60)-(62), reproving [15]). Authors do not claim that birth order becomes physical in non-extending models; they call extending models 'consistent covariant dynamics'.

dependencies: Rudin Theorem 6.4 (complex measures on sigma-algebras have bounded variation)
open_questions: Bounded variation when k_m - k_{m-1} = 1 for m > 1 (Sec. 3.3.1, left open by authors).

record.title: Causal Theories of Time and the Conventionality of Simultaneity
record.version: Noûs 11(3), Symposium on Space and Time (September 1977), pp. 293–300; DOI 10.2307/2214766. The accessed university-hosted PDF is a JSTOR scan of the published article.
record.relevance: Uniqueness result for simultaneity definable from causal connectibility plus an observer worldline; assumption-sensitive result often invoked in presentism debates.
record.limits: Proposition 2 concludes Simo or universal; the non-universal restriction is needed to select Simo. No independent proof audit/formalization, and no unconditional physical or ontological conclusion.
record.section_locator: Sections 1–3: Proposition 1 (p. 296); Proposition 2 statement and proof (pp. 297–299); Proposition 3 (p. 299); definitions of K and observer worldline O (pp. 294–296).
record.assumptions: Minkowski spacetime R⁴ represented by symmetric causal connectibility K and an inertial observer worldline O. Proposition 1 explicitly first-order defines standard simultaneity Simo from K and O. Proposition 2: if S is implicitly definable from K and O, an equivalence relation, and relates a point on O to a point off O, then S is either Simo or universal; adding non-universality selects Simo. Proposition 3: if S is implicitly definable from K alone, is an equivalence relation, and relates two distinct points, then S is universal.
record.conclusion: The paper establishes a mathematical uniqueness/definability result under the stated causal-connectibility, observer-worldline and relation conditions. The causal theory of time supplies a separate philosophical criterion connecting definability with non-conventionality; Malament expresses sympathy with skepticism about that criterion. The result does not unconditionally refute conventionalism or settle temporal ontology.

record.title: Time and Physical Geometry
record.version: The Journal of Philosophy 64(8), 1967, pp.240-247
record.relevance: Influential Rietdijk-Putnam route from special relativity to block-universe/eternalism and critique of objective becoming.
record.section_locator: Full article pp. 240–247, especially thesis (1) and Principle III, “There Are No Privileged Observers” (pp. 241–242); observer-overlap application (pp. 242–243); future-contingent truth discussion (pp. 243–246); transitive-closure argument and abundance-of-observers premise (pp. 246–247). Primary scan route recorded in reading_history.
record.assumptions: Putnam states the ontological thesis that all and only things existing now are real, then invokes Principle III (no privileged observers): if a physical relation R to me-now marks what is real and you-now is real, the same R criterion applies to you-now. R is required to be tenseless, coordinate-independent, and not selected by the initial realness extension. The SR application transfers reality through overlapping observer nows. The broader closure argument uses the transitive closure of observer-coordinate simultaneity plus an abundance-of-observers premise, including physical systems/fields. This ontological bridge is distinct from the geometric transitivity of Einstein simultaneity.
record.conclusion: Putnam argues from the observer-neutral reality-transfer bridge and observer-network closure to reject a past/present/future ontological asymmetry and adopts a block view. This conclusion is not entailed by Lorentz kinematics alone. His future-contingent truth-value discussion is a separate, stronger step and should not be conflated with eternalism or determinism.
record.proof_status: Second-pass audit read the primary paper across pp. 241–247, including Principle III, its application and the general closure discussion; no independent formal proof reconstruction. The earlier first-pass record only inspected pp. 240–242 and used an imprecise transitivity shorthand.
record.open_questions: How defensible is Principle III as an observer-neutral existence bridge, and what restrictions on the observer network/license for closure are justified? How does the future-contingent truth discussion depend on further assumptions?
record.limits: This is Putnam’s argument, not a consequence of SR alone. Preserve the distinction between Principle III, geometric simultaneity transitivity, the later transitive-closure/observer-abundance argument, determinism and future-contingent truth.

record.title: LLMs with in-context learning for Algorithmic Theoretical Physics
record.version: arXiv:2605.08212v1, submitted 2026-05-06; report number IPMU26-0020; license CC BY 4.0
record.locator: Full HTML (arxiv.org/html/2605.08212v1): Sec. 3.2 implementation, Sec. 3.4 evaluation rules, Sec. 3.5 contexts, Sec. 4 results and failure discussions, Sec. 5 conclusions, reference list
record.relevance: Closest public measurement of a single LLM agent with a computer-algebra runtime on novel research-grade problems; its documented failure modes and stage-wise pass/fail rubric are directly reusable for our audit design.
record.limits: Single model (Claude Opus 4-6), single CAS (Maple), 9 problems in one problem family (cosmological perturbation dof counts). Each problem run once; authors say behavior is 'relatively stable' but report no variance estimate. No public code repository named in the paper text read here.
record.setup: Claude Opus 4-6 via API driving a Maple REPL (prettyprint=0), max_tokens=1024, thinking off for main runs, 100-turn cap, expert-written contexts. Problems passed as plain text.
record.quantitative_results: Pass rates by context: 10ex (10 worked examples, 60k tokens) 5/9; 3broad (3 examples, 18k) 5/9; 3tailored (3 examples retargeted at observed failure modes, 24k) 7/9; instruction (2k recipe, no code) 3/9. More turns and Maple restarts correlate with failure. Thinking tokens: little improvement in the five spot-checked runs.
failure_modes_documented: Misinterpretation of problem conventions: 'flat background' read as flat FLRW rather than Minkowski in several problems across contexts (Sec. 4.2, 4.4).
Task abandonment driven by perceived triviality: sRMs solved then abandoned to 'generalize' it, failing (Sec. 4.1).
Incorrect order reduction of higher derivatives when Lagrange-multiplier constraints are forgotten (sRFs, sRi2Fs, sRi2Ft; Sec. 4.1).
Unflagged conditional equivalence: a rewritten action used for sRFs is equivalent only if f''(chi) != 0, used without stating the condition (Sec. 4.2).
Silent branch choice among multiple background solutions (noted across problems; Sec. 4.1).

Unprompted use of training-set knowledge: Starobinsky problem solved by introducing an external scalar via a known trick despite a Jordan-frame restriction (Sec. 4.1); in context 3tailored it followed the required route.
Decision paralysis and minimal tool use with instruction-only context (Sec. 4.4); stuck sessions restart the CAS (up to 7 restarts).
record.evaluation_rubric: Expert pass/fail per staged solution: (1) wrong setup = fail; (2) background equations not substituted is a fail only if it affects the result; (3) perturbations and derivative reduction must be correct; (4) a correct final result with a forgotten subtlety still passes (Sec. 3.4).
reusable_artifacts: Context-design recipe: worked examples beat abstract recipes; a small representative set beats a large one; retarget examples at observed failure modes (Sec. 5.2-5.3, Appendix B recipe).
Stage-wise grading rubric (Sec. 3.4) transferable to any staged derivation.
Turn/restart counts as cheap difficulty telemetry (Fig. 2).
record.authors_claim: Authors evaluate ability 'on par with a first-year graduate student' for this problem family; they explicitly do not claim autonomous physics discovery.
record.proof_status: Empirical evaluation, not a proof; results are the authors' expert gradings.
record.dependencies: Claude Opus 4-6 API; Maple runtime; no other tooling described.
open_questions: Would failure classes transfer to a proof-assistant setting or to the project's Lean-based checks?
No variance across repeated runs; reruns and other models untested in the paper.

record.title: Multi-agent Autoformalization of Tensor Network Theory
record.locator: Main text ('Catching unintended formalizations', 'Discussion'); Supplementary appendices as in HTML v1: A.1 agent-role table, A.2 delegation, C persistent memory, D.1-D.3 orchestration patterns, E paper-to-formalization gap analysis, F cost, H agent definitions
record.relevance: The most complete public multi-agent autoformalization workflow for theoretical physics; its roles, blueprint discipline, gap taxonomy, and stated bottleneck (enforcing mathematical intent) are the primary design inputs for our extraction/translation/counterexample/review roles.
record.limits: Authors' report of their own run; Lean build and review reports not independently rebuilt here (repository inspected at discovery depth only, see meth-tnlean-repo). Costs are the authors' recorded API totals. Formal target is mathematical physics (FT-MPS), not interpretive physics arguments.

workflow_design.roles: leanOrchestrator (expensive tier; decomposition, dispatch, repo access), lean (expensive; proof writing), leanSearch (inexpensive; Mathlib scouting, web/arXiv lookup), leanSimplifier (inexpensive; style and simplification), leanBlueprint (inexpensive; blueprint-Lean sync, bibliography), reviewer (inexpensive; runs on proposed repository changes). Roles were introduced incrementally as bottlenecks appeared (App. A.1).
workflow_design.delegation: Sub-agents run in isolation with fixed role, task instructions, background notes, assigned edit files, and model tier; parallel agents get disjoint file sets (App. A.2, D.1).
orchestration_patterns: Parallel dispatch of 3-5 sub-agents on disjoint file sets, merged and full-built by the orchestrator (D.1).
Scout-then-prove: an inexpensive scout writes a design memo with exact theorem signatures to persistent memory; the expensive prover receives it as read-only context (D.2).
Review-repair cycles converging in 2-3 rounds, with a safety cap of five iterations and no fresh review on each revision to avoid unbounded loops (D.3).
workflow_design.memory: 453 memory files recording tried routes, false statements with counterexamples, and conventions; distilled, project-independent files released under docs/audits/ and docs/paper-gaps/ (App. C).
workflow_design.artifacts: Blueprint (leanblueprint) linking prose statements to Lean declarations via \lean/\leanok tags checked by checkdecls; paper-gap notes published where formal statements diverge from sources.

failure_modes_documented: Weakened statement: agents proved FT-MPS under an extra 'doubly stochastic' gauge (transfer operator both unital and trace-preserving), formally correct but valid for a much smaller tensor class; expensive to remove because later lemmas depended on it (main text 'Weakening of the theorem').

Finite/asymptotic substitution: finite-N statement replaced by an asymptotic norm comparison with wrong hypotheses; agents could not self-patch; humans pointed at the flawed definition (main text 'Finite vs asymptotic limit').
Vacuous statements: proving from hypotheses never satisfied (main text 'Catching unintended formalizations', first paragraph).
Edge cases: absent D>=1, N>=1 assumptions forced Lean through nonphysical cases D=0, N=0 (main text 'Edge cases').
Blueprint-code drift: correct Lean with drifted prose; fixed by explicit synchronization and review criteria (main text 'Lean code-Blueprint alignment').

Resource limits: heartbeat-bounded proofs (default 200,000); factoring a proof cut one from 1,600,000 to 250,000 heartbeats; stale diagnostics need server restart; scouted lemmas can have mismatched types unless inspected (App. D.2).
record.quantitative_results: Core development ~62,000 lines, 2,300 declarations, 233 files inside a ~227,000-line library; six blueprint review rounds for FT-MPS; recorded model-API cost $20,206 whole library, estimated $5,548 for FT-MPS (App. F). Agents found a nonstandard proof of the injective case via Skolem-Noether autonomously (main text).
record.authors_claim: 'We find that the main bottleneck in large-scale autoformalization is enforcing mathematical intent' (abstract); human intervention is strategic (which statement is intended), not tactical (how to prove it).
record.proof_status: Authors report a sorry-free FT-MPS core argument machine-checked in Lean; not rebuilt in this audit.
record.dependencies: Lean 4, Mathlib, TeXRA agent platform; QICLean companion library (per repository README).
open_questions: Do the reviewer prompts released with TNLean catch the defect classes our pilot injects (weakening, vacuity, untraceable premises)?
How much of the role/tool design transfers to non-Lean, interpretive physics comparison tasks where no kernel exists?

record.title: Axioms for physical reasoning: codifying the Seiberg-Witten solution in Lean
record.version: arXiv:2607.06379v1, submitted 2026-07-07; companion repository mrdouglasny/seiberg-witten (not inspected in this pass)
record.locator: HTML v1: Sec. 2 two kinds of formalization; Sec. 4.1 dictionary; Sec. 4.2 H0-H7; Sec. 4.4 what formalizing forces into the open; Sec. 5 checking the axioms; Appendices A-B
record.relevance: The clearest public discipline for separating named physical postulates from checked mathematics, with a working semantic-audit practice: dependency printing, numerical oracle, adversarial statement review, and vacuity hardening. Direct template for our audit procedure.
record.limits: Authors' report; repository and oracle scripts not inspected or rerun here. The physical postulates are argued for, not derived; their justification is external review plus numerics by the authors' own account.
design_principles: Physical postulates are named predicates carried in theorem types (H0-H7); the Lean `axiom` keyword carries only mathematics, so physics never hides in the trusted base (Sec. 2, 4.2, Appendix A).

A single dictionary maps each physical concept to a named mathematical object (e.g., PeriodChart.a/.aD/.tau as coupling; SymplecticReframing as duality); physics enters only through the dictionary (Sec. 4.1).
#print axioms reports the complete trusted base of any result; the genus-one uniqueness theorem's reported footprint is three logical axioms plus two classical covering axioms (Sec. 4.3).
Two kinds of formalization distinguished: proving existing rigorous statements vs. codifying trusted non-rigorous arguments (Sec. 2).
failure_modes_documented: Vacuous hypotheses: first-pass H3 ('there exists a lattice map equal to the Picard-Lefschetz transvection') was true by fiat; hardened to demand an actual deck transformation with covariant central charge. H2 hardened to demand a nonzero charge go massless; H5 pinned to 'exactly 2N' was unsatisfiable at rank 1 and corrected to 'order dividing 2N' with the u -> -u reflection as witness (Sec. 4.4).
A convenient falsehood refused by types: single-valued periods would be vacuous (bounded holomorphic map extends and is constant); data must live on the universal cover (Sec. 4.4).

Family-dependence trap: H6's instanton expansion with free coefficients fits any prepotential at fixed Lambda; content appears only as a weighted-homogeneity clause across the Lambda-family (Sec. 4.4). Heuristic recorded: for every existential inside a hypothesis, ask what stops the witness being reverse-engineered.

Adversarial review beat 62 passing numerical checks: a proposed axiom set failed statement-level review with three gaps (pointwise existence without holomorphic choice, missing boundary limits, an unlabelled parabolic slot); a hyperbolic matrix briefly occupied a parabolic slot passing every property the proofs consumed (Sec. 5, 'Validating a transcription').

The checking apparatus itself erred twice (fractional power on the wrong branch; cycle normalization off by a factor of two), caught by anchor values such as lambda(i)=1/2 before agreeing with Lean (Sec. 5, oracle paragraph).
record.verification_protocol_as_published: Cheapest first: (1) independent numerical oracle in mpmath/numpy sharing no code or authorship with Lean - 9 suites, 278 checks at 30-40 digit precision; authors call a numerical pass 'necessary, not sufficient'; (2) cross-model and self-review against pinned sources, separating 'is it proved?', 'does it say what the source says?', and 'can the intended theorems be derived from it?'; (3) transcription validation with four checks - instantiation, oracle, agreement with independently proved results, adversarial content; (4) the physicist's triangle: independent routes to the same quantity (perturbation theory, Nekrasov instantons, exact periods) attached as a cross-check rather than asserted (Sec. 5).
record.authors_claim: AI's characteristic error in physics derivations is 'a hallucinated assumption, an unphysical premise or a dropped subtlety presented as if derived' (Sec. 1) - the error class our audit targets.
record.proof_status: Authors report sorry-free genus-one theorems with printed axiom footprints; not rebuilt here.
open_questions: Inspect mrdouglasny/seiberg-witten: pin commit, read validate_singcount.py and oracle suites, verify the printed axiom footprints by building.

record.assumptions: Framework: models defined by probabilities over inputs (measurement settings a,b as free variables) and non-input parameters Q; Local Causality decomposed into (i) no future-input dependence (NFID), (ii) lambda-independence, (iii) continuous action (CA). record.conclusion: Authors' claims: any QM-agreeing model must violate Local Causality, but a locally-mediated (CA-satisfying) class survives if NFID is relaxed: intermediate parameters on worldlines may depend on future settings, with all-at-once (boundary-value) solution rather than past-to-future unfolding; no retro-signaling is possible in these models; TSVF and Transactional Interpretation are Type IIB (future-input dependent but not spacetime-localized); superdeterminism violates lambda-independence instead and, in explicit QM-agreeing toy models (Brans 1988; Hall 2016), ends up treating settings as free inputs again, re-entering the framework; Many-Worlds 'outside the framework' recovers a Type IB effective model at the effective-Born-rule level (citing Maudlin 2010); determinism is not a presupposition of Bell's theorem (Bell 1981: 'It is remarkably difficult to get this point across, that determinism is not a presupposition of the analysis').
record.proof_status: Review; authors' framework definitions and toy-model claims read from full TeX. The Bell-theorem derivation itself was read but not re-derived here; its correctness is established literature (consistent with Griffiths 1984/Cramer 1986 bibliographies linking ABL/Bell lines).
